The focal object is the numerical finite-sample absolute-risk frontier for the ordinary ATE with public treatment and covariates and an unknown rough propensity. A centered spatial higher-order construction must attain that frontier on the entire stipulated class, with original-likelihood converses against every randomized estimator. Honest connected-interval length and uniform transitions in the public reporting power are companion outputs. Their rates and equality are questions rather than assumptions.
